inputs.wacc_rationale: NZD-built, itemized: NZ 10y govt ~4.5% + 5.0% ERP x beta 0.9 = ~9.0% core cost of equity; + 1.25% NZX small-cap illiquidity premium (mkt cap ~NZ$645m; the Jun-2026 Ngai Tahu 9.6% block was ~1.3x a full year's trading volume); + 1.0% structural biological/regulatory tail premium (single-site Big Glory Bay salmon under a hard nitrogen cap with marine-heatwave exposure; ministerial TACC discretion over the quota asset -- ORH 3B cut 4,752t->2,321t with a proposed Jun-2026 spawning closure, uncompensated) => cost of equity ~11.25%. After-tax cost of debt ~4.5% (6.3% pre-tax x 0.72); E/V 87%, D/V 13% => WACC 10.3%, rounded to 10.5%. Risk charged once: commodity-price and margin CYCLICALITY is priced in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, NOT in WACC; the WACC premia cover only illiquidity and the non-cyclical structural tails no scenario path models. Same 10.5% in all three scenarios (owner-fcf.md s7f).
notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, 10-year component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods SKILL routing: operating company, non-US cyclical -- section 7 adaptations applied). Fresh build; no prior SAN.NZ DCF and no MEMORY.md entry.

OWNER FCF: last_fcf = reported FCF 112.854 - SBC 0.219 - lease payments (principal 14.324 + lease interest 2.088, note 19) = 96.22. Interest income ($1.5m) NOT stripped: Sanford is a net-DEBT company, so there is no cash pile being separately added to EV (owner-fcf.md s1b applies only to net-cash names).

LEASE TREATMENT B (one treatment, stated): full lease cash cost (principal + interest, 2.8% of revenue) charged inside the flows via lease_cost_pct; lease liabilities ($41.4m) excluded from net debt. Short-term/variable ACE and property leases ($9.6m FY2025) are already expensed inside EBITDA and need no adjustment.

PEAK WARNING -- FY2025/last_fcf IS NOT THE MODEL BASE: FY2025 owner FCF of $96m embeds ~$36m of working-capital release and a ~$22m cash-tax underpayment (cash tax paid $3.3m vs ~$25m accrued on PBT $90.0m; H1 FY2026 paid $17.5m as the catch-up). H1 FY2026 OCF collapsed to $13.7m (from $49.6m) on frozen mussel inventory build. The DCF is component-built: year-1 owner FCF ~$74m fading to a mid-cycle ~$41-50m at a 20% EBITDA margin, 28% cash tax and 6% capex -- the mid-cycle remedy applied ex ante, not after a sanity-check trip.
CASH TAX: modelled at the 28% NZ statutory rate in all years and scenarios. FY2025's 3.7% cash rate is timing, already unwinding in H1 FY2026.

CAPEX NORMALIZED UP: FY2025 capex $22.5m (3.9% of revenue) and H1 FY2026 $6.7m are deferral-level lows against a 10-year average ~8% of revenue and total D&A of 6.1%; base ramps 3.5%->6.0% by year 5 (aging fleet, 5-year dry-dock cycles, vessels 30+ years old).

BIOLOGICAL FAIR-VALUE GAINS EXCLUDED: projected EBITDA margins are ex-bio-gain cash margins. H1 FY2026 reported EBITDA (30.3% margin) includes a $17.5m non-cash biological-asset fair-value gain; ex-gain ~23.8%. FY2025 full-year bio FV change was +$5.4m.
NCI: negligible -- profit attributable to NCI was -$2k (FY2025) / +$15k (FY2024); no NCI adjustment made (charge-once rule satisfied trivially).
SBC-ZERO: SBC rows kept explicit at 0.0% (house rule); street basis = house basis, band_position null.
EPS UNITS: the Metrics CSV stores EPS in CENTS (FY2025 = 68.1c = NZ$0.681). All per-share dollar figures here are derived as net_income / shares, never from the CSV EPS column.

ANCHOR VINTAGE: net debt is the latest (31-Mar-2026) balance sheet while year 1 projects the full FY2026 flow; H1 cash generation is thus partly double-counted AGAINST the valuation (H1 inventory build raised net debt) -- conservative direction, and management guides further debt reduction.

TTM cross-check (FY2025 + H1 FY2026 - H1 FY2025): revenue $568.3m, adj EBITDA $151.4m ($131.8m ex bio gains, 23.2%), NPAT $72.1m, OCF $99.4m, capex $13.4m, owner FCF ~$69.6m -- close to the component-built year-1 $74m.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR of 23.2% is a trough-to-peak recovery artifact (FY2020 COVID NPAT $22.4m -> FY2025 record $63.7m) and diverges >30% from revenue (4.5%) and equity (3.9%) CAGRs. Through-cycle revenue CAGR is 2.8%; the QMS caps wildcatch volume and the nitrogen cap holds salmon flat, so growth above ~3-4% requires mussel expansion plus price.
historical_growth.notes: FCF 3yr/5yr CAGRs are null: the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - lease payments) is negative at the FY2020 and FY2022 base years (-$35m and -$21m). The 10yr figure (FY2015 $38.9m -> FY2025 $96.2m, +9.5%/yr) is peak-to-peak and NOT a trend -- owner FCF averaged roughly ZERO over FY2016-FY2023. SBC adjustment is immaterial to every CAGR (SBC <0.05% of revenue throughout).

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 revenue -3.5% (H1 -5.5% on lower mussel/scampi volumes; softer H2 comp), then 2-3.5% growth as the Western Firth of Thames mussel consent (first harvest ~Mar-2027), the new farming vessel, record SPATnz spat and reactivated water space add volume against flat wildcatch (QMS-capped, ORH 3B cut) and flat salmon (nitrogen cap). Roughly half the Back-to-Basics margin gain proves structural: ex-bio-gain EBITDA margin fades from ~23.5% to a 20% mid-cycle (decade average 15.7%, FY2025 24.1%) as FY2025's exceptional Havelock mussel yields and hoki/orange-roughy pricing normalise -- management itself guides FY2026 mussel yields 'above average' but below FY2025. Capex normalises 3.5%->6.0% of revenue (aging fleet, dry-dock cycles); cash tax 28%; each incremental revenue dollar absorbs 20c of working capital. Terminal growth 2.0%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Back to Basics is a durable operating-model reset, not a harvest of easy wins: SKU rationalisation, pull-based supply and Timaru/Havelock yield gains hold the ex-gain EBITDA margin at ~23%; hoki and orange roughy pricing stays strong (TACC scarcity), scampi recovers with China, and the mussel pipeline (Western Firth, new vessel, 2044 permit extension, unused water space) compounds revenue ~4-5% mid-decade. The wildcatch strategic review monetises or fixes sub-scale assets; capex discipline holds at 5% with the balance sheet moving to net cash within the decade. Terminal growth 2.5%.
scenario_narratives.bear: The record was weather and price, not structure: mussel yields mean-revert (FY2026 inventory build already signals demand softness -- H1 OCF $13.7m), scampi/China stays weak, NZD strengthens, and a marine heatwave or algal event at single-site Big Glory Bay -- the risk that has repeatedly hit Marlborough competitors -- takes a salmon harvest. Further TACC cuts follow ORH 3B, shrinking Timaru throughput. Margins revert to the 16% decade average, revenue contracts then crawls at ~1%, and the aging fleet forces 6.5% capex. Owner FCF ~$20m/yr: on flows the equity is worth ~$1.96 -- the DCF floor; actual downside is cushioned by the quota/NTA asset backing ($7.92 book NTA, quota at historic cost) IF the board monetised assets, which this flows-only model deliberately does not credit. Terminal growth 1.5%.

entry_price.note: Entry price per scenario = (PV of 10y owner FCF at 15% + TV (WACC-Gordon, 13x cap) discounted at 15% - net debt) / shares; probability-weighted with the same 25/50/25 weights. At $6.90 the 15% hurdle is met only well below even the base entry price of $3.34.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% (house default 15%) because the tails are real and uninsurable: single-site salmon under a hard nitrogen cap with demonstrated sector-wide marine-heatwave mortality, ministerial TACC discretion over the core asset (ORH 3B just cut 51% uncompensated), and record FY2025 results that management itself partly attributes to unrepeatable mussel yields -- with H1 FY2026 cash conversion (OCF $13.7m vs NPAT $42.4m) already wobbling. Bull trimmed to 25% (default 35%) because it needs pricing, yields, mussel volume AND capex discipline to persist simultaneously. Weights sum to 1.0.
probability_weighted.band_note: SBC-zero filer: house and street bases coincide (SBC $0.2m, <0.05% of revenue), so the accounting-regime band collapses to a point and band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (adjustment immaterial: SBC <0.05% of revenue). September FY-end closes from Yahoo 11y monthly series, bar-start NZT convention verified (the bar opening 1-Sep holds the 30-Sep close). Net debt = bank borrowings - cash, leases excluded, consistent with treatment B. Adjusted-EBITDA (company measure) used for EV/EBITDA. These will not match Yahoo GAAP screeners.
sanity_check.outlier_rationale: FY2020/FY2021 COVID-depressed earnings (NPAT $22.4m/$16.2m) and FY2023 impairment-hit NPAT ($10.0m after $14.8m PP&E impairment) distort earnings multiples; kept in the table for visibility, excluded from averages.
sanity_check.peak_fcf_test: last_fcf $96.2m IS a peak -- 6.4x the FY2016-FY2025 owner-FCF median (~$15m) and the highest in the series. It TRIPS the peak-earnings test in isolation, which is exactly why the model never capitalizes it: the component build starts year 1 at ~$74m and fades to a $41-50m mid-cycle (20% EBITDA margin, 28% cash tax, 6% capex). The structural-WACC test is also pre-applied (+2.25% of itemized premia in the 10.5% WACC).
sanity_check.diagnosis: PASS. Implied base-case multiples are below history on every axis: P/E 6.8x vs 14.5x ex-outlier average; P/B 0.58x vs 1.28x max; EV/EBITDA 3.8x vs 12.4x max; P/Sales 0.74x vs 1.51x max. Base upside is -32.9% with the price ($6.90) in the upper half of the 10y range ($3.76-$8.30) after an ~80% 12-month re-rating. The DCF is more conservative than any multiple the market has paid -- the market at $6.90 is pricing roughly the bull case ($7.55, EBITDA margins held at ~23% with 5% capex forever).
sanity_check.fix_applied: none required -- the two most likely trip causes (peak-FCF extrapolation, structural WACC understatement) were remediated ex ante in the component build and the itemized WACC.

valuation_philosophy: Flows, not assets, and mid-cycle, not peak. Sanford's FY2025 record ($63.7m NPAT, $112.9m FCF) sits on a decade in which NPAT ranged $10-56m and owner FCF averaged roughly zero; FY2025 cash flow was further flattered by a working-capital release and a $22m cash-tax underpayment that H1 FY2026 is already repaying (OCF $13.7m). The model therefore credits roughly half the Back-to-Basics margin gain as structural (20% mid-cycle EBITDA vs 15.7% decade average and 24.1% FY2025), normalizes capex up to 6% of revenue against a fleet whose D&A alone is 6.1%, and taxes at 28%. On those flows the weighted IV is $4.69 against a $6.90 price: the market is paying ~90% of the way to the bull case, i.e. for margin persistence AND capex discipline holding indefinitely. Two honest caveats cut the other way. First, the quota book (~$486m, ~19.8% of national QMS quota) is carried at historic cost, so the $7.92 book NTA understates replacement asset value -- but Sanford has closed above 1.3x book exactly never in ten years and above 1.0x only in FY2016-FY2019, because the market (correctly, on this decade's evidence) discounts the earnings power of those assets rather than their price; an asset-backing argument cannot justify a multiple the stock has never traded at, and this model does not use one. Second, the bear case ($1.96) values flows only and ignores the asset floor a monetisation would realise -- that asymmetry is why bear is weighted 25% rather than higher. Investment framing: a well-run cyclical priced for its best case; the 15% hurdle entry is $3.37 weighted, and even a 9% required return only reaches $5.18 on base assumptions.
